articles.title: Making Postgres queues scale
articles.summary: Postgres-backed queues can be optimized to handle large workloads by using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED queries and adjusting transaction isolation levels. This approach allows multiple workers to dequeue workflows concurrently without contention, enabling scalability beyond ~100 workflows per second. By understanding how Postgres provides primitive locking clauses like FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, developers can take advantage of this optimization technique to build more scalable queue systems.

articles.title: So you want to use plants to reduce CO₂
articles.summary: Plants can potentially help reduce carbon dioxide levels in a home or office by converting it into oxygen through photosynthesis, but this process is limited and will not be easily replicated without significant technological advancements. Real plants require energy to perform photosynthesis, which they obtain from sunlight, and the amount of energy required is substantial. In practice, plants use around 551 watts of pure red light per hour, which can make a room feel like it's emitting a significant amount of heat. This highlights the need for more efficient lighting solutions that can effectively neutralize CO2 without compromising on comfort or aesthetics.
